object_description: mighty square building with a cross-shaped public passage and a roof garden
design_condition: the square solitaire is placed precisely in the urban space so that the resulting outdoor spaces respond differently to each surrounding structure, with an arcade to the street, a square at the church and a green arena to the villa district

positive: The authors place a mighty square building precisely in the urban space
The project was developed in a coherent and consistent manner from its historical reference
The church remains standing, is adequately adapted and stands its ground next to the main building
The outdoor spaces all respond in a differentiated and precise manner to the surrounding structures
The arcade leads to the busy street, the square with the church to the old town
The green outdoor space designed as an arena relates to the gardens of the villa district
Despite the size and presence of the volume the open spaces appear appropriate and urban
The use of the attic with an attractively designed roof garden is welcomed
Inside, the building develops along a differentiated spatial sequence of different main rooms
The interior diversity is more pronounced than expected from the outside
Natural lighting is guaranteed via different systems of skylights
The non-directional 8.4 metre column grid promises a high level of flexibility
The revised expression makes the building lighter and more finely structured
The idea of flexibility and the desired spatial relationships are implemented very well in the large rooms
On the upper floors a clearly recognisable spatial reference supports interdisciplinary exchange
The volume is compact and rationally constructed
Efficient building technology and natural night cooling via the atriums promise a solid sustainability contribution
Construction costs are within the specifications
A precisely derived design that is coherent in all areas with an appropriate density of use
negative: Whether the cross-shaped passageway would actually be accepted and used by the public remains to be seen
Barrier-free permeability is severely limited by the staged topography
The roof areas heavily occupied by photovoltaics conflict with the extensive green roofs
The terminology of town hall, market square and vestibule seems a bit far-fetched and artificial
The very specific architecture and spatial structure contradict the idea of flexibility
The design remains lingering in history through its typology, references and analogies
The architecture is too heavy, too static and too introverted for a university seeking dialogue
The clear differentiation between usage and access areas was severely impaired in the cleanup stage
This made the spatial structure unclear and caused major escape route problems
Neither the urban attitude nor the expression correspond to how the institution wants to present itself
